races.title: State Senate, District 31
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Dana Caudill Jones
cands.bio: Republican state senator for North Carolina's 31st District (Forsyth and Stokes counties) since January 2025. Co-leads Caudill's Commercial Electric in Kernersville with her husband. Previously served on the Kernersville Board of Aldermen and eight years on the Winston-Salem/Forsyth County school board.

endorsements.text: The Winston-Salem Journal endorsed her in the 2014 primary and general elections for the Winston-Salem/Forsyth County school board.

cands.gaps: The pages reviewed show no stated positions or actions by Jones on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns or abortion. The list of bills she has sponsored was empty on the page we could read. Her record on school choice is also missing, apart from a 2014 statement about teacher pay. We found no data-center or development statements, no documented controversies and no foreign ties. Her birthplace and upbringing come only from her own campaign website, and we found no independent source or birth year. We did not find an independent source for her private-sector work history beyond her campaign site and Ballotpedia.

local.label: Roots 100: Her campaign website says she was born and raised in Kernersville, NC, and still works in her family's Kernersville business; this is her own account.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Sitting state senator since January 2025. Previously served on the Kernersville Board of Aldermen (about ten years, with a stint as Mayor Pro Tem) and on the Winston-Salem/Forsyth County school board (eight years, including time as chair). Co-owner and leader of Caudill's Commercial Electric, a family business in Kernersville.
qual.why: She has prior legislative service in the state Senate, years in local elected office with budget responsibility, and business ownership. Committee assignments and board service were not counted.
qual.label: She has prior legislative service in the state Senate, years in local elected office with budget responsibility, and business ownership. Committee assignments and board service were not counted.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In a 2014 UNC-TV voter guide statement for a school board race, she said teachers and staff should earn salaries comparable to their peers nationwide and that she would push for better teacher pay. This covers teacher pay only; it says nothing on vouchers, charters or school choice.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

roots.summary: Her campaign website says she was born and raised in Kernersville, NC, and still works in her family's Kernersville business; this is her own account.

cands.name: Andy Bowline
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina Senate District 31 in 2026. Lives in Winston-Salem. Stay-at-home dad and former health tech CEO who co-founded a health tech company, and has worked as a software developer and nonprofit consultant. Holds an MBA from Wake Forest University.

endorsements.text: Progressive Caucus of the North Carolina Democratic Party
NC Public School Champions (Sway voting group by Taylor, PublicEdTay)

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Bowline was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. He has held no elected office, so there is no record of actions in office. His campaign site raises concerns about a data center near Walnut Cove and its power use, but the page we had didn't state a position on banning, pausing or approving data centers. We couldn't read the site's deeper pages on data centers and the full plans. We found no stated positions from him on growth and land protection, foreign or investor land buying, immigration and H-1B, policing, guns or abortion.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Co-founded a health tech company and served as its CEO, worked as a software developer and nonprofit consultant, and earned an MBA from Wake Forest. He has held no elected office.
qual.why: He has business founder and manager experience, which fits the middle tier. He has no legislative service and no documented law, policy or budget career.
qual.label: He has business founder and manager experience, which fits the middle tier. He has no legislative service and no documented law, policy or budget career.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says he would freeze expansion of the Opportunity Scholarship voucher program until existing public schools are funded, and criticizes vouchers as mostly going to families already in private school.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Says he would expand property tax relief so reassessments don't push longtime homeowners out of their homes.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised
